snippet.title: GTA 6's Perfect Reviews Make NO SENSE!
snippet.description:
GTA 6 has a reported 99 Metacritic score, but after finally playing Rockstar Games' biggest release, I'm starting to question whether Grand Theft Auto VI actually deserves all this praise!

Gaming critics are calling GTA 6 a masterpiece, but my experience on PlayStation 5 has been VERY different.

The graphics and open world are incredible, but the mission design, slow pacing, and 30 FPS console performance have left me seriously disappointed.

I originally planned to wait for GTA 6 on PC, but the overwhelming reviews convinced me to jump in early. Now I'm wondering if I should've waited!

Is GTA 6 really one of the greatest games ever made, or has the gaming media completely overhyped Rockstar's latest release?

The reported 99 Metacritic score still needs independent verification, but my criticism is about the gap between the hype and my actual gameplay experience.

**Does GTA 6 deserve a perfect review score, or are critics giving Rockstar a free pass?**

snippet.title: You'll Play GTA 6 at Least 3 Times
snippet.description:
Can Jason cheat on Lucia in GTA 6? Rockstar has never said you can, but Rockstar North's Rob Nelson says Jason and Lucia start the game wanting to give their relationship another shot, and that as the game goes on it's yours to keep or yours to lose, with how you treat it changing how their story plays out.

In your first run you keep it, so you spend time together, walk the beach and answer every text, until they leave the clothing store holding hands, and in your second run you lose it by ignoring them, which Nelson says can hurt the relationship, while they still stay partners in crime no matter what.

In your third run the romance never starts at all, because it's optional, and Nelson's own advice is that if you're not into it, you don't have to bother, so they're just two criminals working together.

Nelson finished his run in about 80 hours with some side missions, so three runs like his is about 240 hours of GTA 6, and he says lots of choices, big and small, shape the ending, which means your first run only shows you one version of Jason and Lucia.

Sources:
Edge's GTA VI preview, Rob Nelson on the relationship ("yours to keep or yours to lose"), via GTAVice: https://www.gtavice.net/news/gta-vi-edge-preview-reveals-huge-new-details-on-gameplay-police-relationships-and-more
